packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-10 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text before I began. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files. (The packet directory listing showed a packet.json file name; I did not read it.)

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 1, from overview image-001.jpg)
- Single leaf of paper, upright, one column, about 37 written lines; text block frame-ruled in drypoint/lead (vertical bounding lines left and right, horizontal line at top). Scale bar below (about 16 cm). A library stamp, upside down/mirrored, at the upper right corner outside the text block (not part of the text).
- Damage: holes and losses along the left edge (lines ~2, ~9-12, ~15-16), a large hole at right centre (lines ~26-28), losses at lower right corner (lines ~31-35). Bottom line partly cut/abraded.
- Hand: small, rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive (scholastic Latin), brown ink. No enlarged initials or rubrics visible; paragraph marks (a C-shaped pilcrow) occur within lines, e.g. line ~8 start, ~10 end, ~17, ~24, ~26, ~29, ~32. A small mark in the left margin around line ~21 (possibly a pen trial or a number).
- No running title, no interlinear or marginal glosses seen on the overview. Tentative interpretation: continuous prose (commentary/question-style treatise); the frequent abbreviations look like "fallacia", "elenchi", "sophistica", but that is a reading to check on the tiles, not an identification.
- Text begins mid-sentence at top (leaf is part of a larger work).

CONVENTIONS: graphemic rendering of abbreviations with my proposed expansions in parentheses; "?" after an uncertain reading; [illegible] where I could not resolve. "2" = the 2-shaped sign in this hand (probably "et" or a "-um/secundum" sign; I leave it as "2" where unsure). "9" = con-/com- sign. Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile image. The hand is very cursive and heavily abbreviated; readings below are low-confidence word-by-word.
